target_customer: Web developers and agencies who wanted to ship iOS and Android apps from an HTML5 codebase; freemium with attribution and paid white label tiers
problem: Web developers had to learn native stacks to ship mobile apps; Trigger.io (Forge) wrapped HTML and JavaScript in a fast native bridge with native UI elements.
business_model: Freemium developer platform with paid monthly subscription tiers
product_category: Cross platform mobile app development framework

founders.name: James Brady
founders.background_notes: Listed on the YC page. SiliconIndia names him as co-founder.

founders.name: Amir Nathoo
previous_startups: WebMynd (co-founder and CEO, same company renamed)
founders.background_notes: Quoted as co-founder in TechCrunch January 2012; not on the YC page.

competitors.name: PhoneGap
competitors.what: Wraps HTML apps in a native web view; the main rival named by TechCrunch

competitors.name: Appcelerator Titanium
competitors.what: Cross platform native app framework using JavaScript

technical_complexity.rationale: A native to JavaScript bridge across iOS, Android and browsers with cloud builds and native UI modules needed deep platform knowledge; the company claimed a bridge up to 5 times faster than PhoneGap on Android (vendor claim).

defensibility.rationale: Apps built on the framework were tied to it, but PhoneGap was free and open source and Adobe backed it.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition of Trigger found. Dealroom, a single database, says James Brady and Amir Nathoo joined Square by 2013.

market_need_then: HTML5 mobile tooling was an active category in 2012 with PhoneGap and Appcelerator already used, and investors put 1 million dollars into Trigger in January 2012.

branding.domain_note: Used trigger.io; the YC page lists trigger.io. The site returned HTTP 503 when checked.
branding.brand_signature: Forge, the build tool and framework name

rebrands.why: Seedtable says Trigger.io was formerly WebMynd and TechCrunch says Trigger was previously WebMynd; the date and reason are not found

branding.community_and_virality: Technical community use with Stack Overflow questions and docs; a CEO Hacker News post in 2012 compared it with PhoneGap. No merch found.

brand_strength.rationale: Known among mobile developers and used in comparison sites, but a generic name and no strong brand assets found.

pivots.to: Trigger, a cross platform mobile development framework
pivots.why: Not stated in sources; TechCrunch January 2012 notes only that Trigger was previously WebMynd

outcome_analysis: Trigger was the later form of WebMynd, a YC Winter 2008 company, and became a cross platform mobile framework that raised about 1 million dollars from SV Angel, Paul Graham and others in January 2012. The YC page says 1.8 million dollars total. The directory lists it inactive but no shutdown note, cause or acquisition is public, so the cause of its inactive status is not public and no failure factors are asserted.
notes: Funding gap: the YC page says 1.8 million dollars in seed funding while TechCrunch reports a 1 million dollar round and Seedtable lists 400 thousand dollars total; about 0.8 million dollars is unaccounted for and no date, amount or investor for it was found (Dealroom adds Streamlined Ventures, Hinge Capital and 500 Global with a range of 1.8 to 1.99 million, a single database). SiliconIndia names a Sahil Jain as co-founder; no company source confirms him so he is not listed. The Dealroom claim that Brady and Nathoo joined Square is single source. Competition is dated to the January 2012 product launch, not the 2008 YC batch, because Trigger the mobile framework did not exist in 2008; WebMynd era competition is not recorded. Trigger.dev and Trigify results are different companies.
